en: Eat Along the Route: Black Eggs, Amazake, and the Dinner Clock
zh: 沿途怎么吃：黑鸡蛋、甘酒与晚餐时钟
ja: 道中で何を食べるか：黒たまご、甘酒、夕食の時計

p.src: Places to eat are spread along the Hakone route, and each stop serves a different purpose. Board-steamed kamaboko is a taste of the Odawara gateway; a black egg is an Owakudani snack; Gora, the museum, or Lake Ashi can provide a proper seated lunch; Amasake Chaya is an old-road rest; and a ryokan dinner included in the booking has a start time that cannot simply drift later. The diagram puts these stops in travel order without asking anyone to visit them all. Choose the day's one essential meal first, then add only the snacks that lie on the route actually travelled. On a ryokan day, dinner is the endpoint, so earlier stops must respect the agreed arrival time. On a day trip, the last useful transport is the endpoint. This food clock is neither a restaurant ranking nor a universal schedule. It prevents a common mistake: tasting several things without ever eating lunch.

caption.zh: 食物节点按作用排列，不按比例，也不要求全部经过。先选一处真正吃午饭，再加入顺路小吃；住店日以预约晚餐为终点。
caption.ja: 食の地点を役割順に並べた図で、縮尺図でも全地点を回る指示でもない。昼食を一か所決め、経路上の間食だけを加え、宿泊日は予約した夕食を終点にする。
caption.en: Food stops are arranged by role, not to scale and not as a compulsory route. Choose one real lunch, add only on-route snacks, and make booked ryokan dinner the endpoint on an overnight day.

p.src: Choose the lunch anchor before going uphill; lunch itself need not be eaten before the climb. Pick one: sit down after the museum, eat a proper meal during the Owakudani transfer, or look for clearly identified Lake Ashi wakasagi by the lake. Then check reservations, weather, and transport. When staying on a dinner-and-breakfast plan, take one complete lunch even if it is slightly early instead of assembling a late meal from snacks. On a day trip, lunch can sit beside the main visit, provided the return still has a margin. Carry a small amount of food that is reliably suitable for your own diet, plus water, for a suspension, queue, or sell-out; there is no need to turn the whole day into a cold picnic. Do not force a full museum visit, the nature trail, a lakeside lunch, Amasake Chaya, and a punctual ryokan dinner into one ideal chain. Removing one stop is usually better than rushing to a connection hungry.

p.src: At Owakudani, first ask whether today's route already passes through. If it does, black eggs fit a short stop after changing cabins. If the ropeway is suspended, the area is closed, or the route does not go there, do not make a detour for one bag of eggs. As checked on 20 August 2026, the operator still lists four eggs for JPY 500 and warns that they can sell out and that sales hours vary by season. One bag gives each of the four guides an egg, enough to taste it and inspect the black shell. Once peeled, it looks like an ordinary boiled egg. What belongs to the place is the shell blackened by the geothermal water and steam, together with the local story linking Enmei Jizo and the number seven. This is an easy snack to share, not lunch. A seated hot meal requires its own stop; eating a black egg does not replace it.

caption.zh: 一袋四枚黑鸡蛋：黑色只在蛋壳，剥开后仍是普通熟鸡蛋。把它当作大涌谷的短点心，不当作健康食品。
caption.ja: 一袋四個の黒たまご。黒いのは殻で、むけば普通のゆで卵である。大涌谷での短い軽食として味わい、健康食品とは考えない。
caption.en: One four-egg pack: the shell is black, while the peeled egg remains an ordinary boiled egg. Treat it as a short Owakudani snack, not a health product.

p.src: Choose one anchor for the substantial lunch. At the Open-Air Museum, a quick cafe break, a seated restaurant meal, and eating your own food in a designated area consume different amounts of viewing time; decide before entering. Owakudani has separate options for a sit-down meal and a quick snack, but operation, weather, and transport can change the stop. If the route reaches Lake Ashi, ask whether the restaurant has wakasagi explicitly identified as caught in the lake. Kanagawa records that the fish was introduced from Lake Kasumigaura in 1918, later became Hakone's town fish, and entered the Kanagawa Brand register in 2025. That history matters only when the stated origin matches. Wakasagi may be fried, served as tempura, marinated as nanbanzuke, or simmered as kanroni; verify origin and stock first. Eat properly at one of these three anchors rather than crossing the mountain to compare menus.

ja: せんきゅうひゃくじゅうはちねん

caption.zh: 炸公鱼与南蛮渍把芦之湖放进午饭。点餐时先确认是否为芦之湖产，再问当天仍有哪种做法。
caption.ja: わかさぎのフライと南蛮漬けで芦ノ湖を昼食に取り入れる。注文前に芦ノ湖産かを確かめ、その日に用意できる料理を聞く。
caption.en: Fried wakasagi and nanbanzuke bring Lake Ashi to lunch. Confirm Lake Ashi origin first, then ask which preparation is available that day.

p.src: Amasake Chaya is convenient only when the old road or a route K bus is already part of the day. On arrival, check the next departure, direction, and destination, then order to fit the time available. This shop's amazake is made from rice koji and rice, with no added sugar or alcohol. A drink with the same name elsewhere may use different ingredients, so ask again. Chikara-mochi is charcoal grilled and served two pieces to a plate in soy-and-nori isobe, green-soybean uguisu, and limited black sesame. One cup each and a shared plate give the four guides time to sit, warm their hands, and organize the next leg. It is a rest, not lunch. Anyone walking the stone-paved road needs a complete meal elsewhere and should not miss the bus departure that fits the onward journey for the sake of extending the tea-house stop.

caption.zh: 米曲甘酒与一盘力饼正好构成旧路上的短休息。这里的甘酒不加糖，也不含酒精；返程班次仍要先查。
caption.ja: 米麹の甘酒と力餅一皿で、旧街道の短い休憩にする。ここの甘酒は砂糖不使用、ノンアルコール。帰りの便は先に確かめる。
caption.en: Rice-koji amazake and one plate of chikara-mochi make a route-sized rest. This shop's drink has no added sugar or alcohol; check the onward bus first.

p.src: Back in Odawara, the food story shifts from volcano and mountain road to the processing craft of a coastal city. Odawara's historic-landscape plan records a local tradition that kamaboko production began in the Tenmei era, around 1781-1789, when coastal catches were increasing; expanding transport widened the market after the Meiji period. The characteristic form of Odawara kamaboko is fish paste shaped on a wooden board and steamed to a fine-grained, springy texture. A hot fried fish-cake snack near the station suits a short transfer, but it is not the same board-steamed form. At a clean workshop bench, the four guides watch paste being shaped on boards and compare the cut texture. During a transfer, taste a small portion near the station or buy only what can be stored as its label requires. A visit to production and exhibits at Kazamatsuri needs its own time block; do not add it casually before the first climb into Hakone.

yī qī bā yī zhì yī qī bā jiǔ nián
ja: いたつきむしかまぼこ

caption.zh: 小田原鱼糕的基本形态，是把鱼糜整形在木板上蒸熟。短换乘可在站区尝一小份；看制作过程则要给风祭另留时间。
caption.ja: 小田原かまぼこの基本形は、魚のすり身を板に成形して蒸すもの。短い乗り換えなら駅周辺で少量を味わい、製造を見るなら風祭に別の時間を取る。
caption.en: Odawara's defining kamaboko form is fish paste shaped on a board and steamed. Taste a small portion near the station during a transfer; allow a separate Kazamatsuri stop to see production.

p.src: Whether the room plan includes dinner determines how the food route ends. When dinner is included, treat it as the final meal already reserved: eat one complete lunch, add no more than one or two route snacks, and stop sightseeing in time for the property's agreed arrival window. In the illustration, the four guides sit down at the confirmed time while dishes arrive in sequence. This shows that dinner takes time; it does not claim that every property serves one identical form of “Hakone kaiseki.” A room-only plan requires a separate dinner arrangement. The word ryokan does not guarantee walk-in meal service that evening. If transport is delayed, contact the property first, learn what can still be provided, and then remove snacks, a detour, or the pre-dinner bath. Food eaten earlier in the day does not make a missed dinner booking harmless.

caption.zh: 一泊二食的晚餐是预约，不是随时开放的餐厅。按开始时段入席；过敏和饮食限制要在订房前写清楚并取得答复。
caption.ja: 一泊二食の夕食は予約の一部で、いつでも入れる食堂ではない。開始時刻に席へ着き、アレルギーや食事制限は予約前に書面で伝えて回答を得る。
caption.en: Dinner in a two-meal stay is an appointment, not an all-hours restaurant. Sit down at the agreed time, and disclose allergies or dietary restrictions in writing before booking.

p.src: Ask about exact ingredients. For kamaboko, read the label and storage instructions. For fried wakasagi, ask about batter, oil, and sauce. For mochi, ask about soy sauce, soybean, or sesame. At a ryokan, ask about stock, seasoning, substitutions, and cross-contact. Recipes vary; a dish name is not enough. Raise ordinary dietary restrictions early. For a serious allergy, obtain written confirmation before booking or buying about whether both the ingredient and cross-contact can be avoided. A Chinese-Japanese-English ingredient card or the word-card device aids the conversation; it does not replace confirmation from the kitchen. If staff cannot confirm, change the dish, plan, or lodging before food reaches the table.

p.src: When a planned shop is closed or transport changes, protect the next leg first. If the ropeway cannot reach Owakudani, let the black eggs go. If a boat or bus change makes lakeside lunch impractical, eat at the last transport hub that still has real choices. If the next route K bus does not suit the journey, shorten or remove the tea-house stop. Do not backtrack across the mountain to chase one dish, and do not leave fresh fish or kamaboko requiring refrigeration in a bag for hours. Backup food can carry the group through one delay; it is not a replacement for lunch. Before leaving a counter, read the storage label, use-by information, and whether the package can be carried safely for the rest of the journey. On a ryokan day, test every substitute against one final condition: can the group still arrive as agreed and eat the dinner already booked?

p.src: Day trip: eat breakfast before the climb; choose the museum, Owakudani, or Lake Ashi for lunch; share black eggs only if they are on the route; and eat dinner after leaving the mountain. Ryokan night: eat a proper early lunch; choose either black eggs or the tea house, or skip both; stop sightseeing for the arrival window; and dine at the ryokan. Old-road day: carry water and a small backup snack; walk a suitable stone-paved section; treat amazake and mochi as a rest; and eat a full meal before or after. Taste Odawara kamaboko before the climb or buy it on return. A Kazamatsuri production visit needs its own time. A workable day has three outcomes: everyone eats a real meal, no snack costs a connection, and the ryokan is not left waiting.
